description: A petroleum system: a mature source-rock kitchen (Lopatin TTI) charging structural traps with seal and reservoir that formed before generation ended; the reservoirs feed Create: Diesel Generators.
notes: Lopatin TTI thresholds 15 (oil onset), 75 (peak), 160 (end of oil): Waples 1980, AAPG Bulletin 64:916 (abstract via OSTI; a journal fact, not USGS). USGS reports use close values: TTI 10 ≈ Ro 0.6 % for onset and TTI ≈ 160 ≈ Ro 1.3 % for thermogenic gas (PP 1698 p. 22), an oil window of TTI 10–180 (OFR 88-450-G). See crates/deeptime-core/data/usgs/petroleum.json.

Field size: the example of USGS World Petroleum Assessment 2000 (DDS-60), Niger Delta Agbada Reservoirs assessment unit 71920101, undiscovered oil fields: median 12 MMBO from the data form; p90 ≈ 2.4 and p10 ≈ 89 MMBO measured off the USGS histogram (the digitiser's log interpolation). Converted to tonnes at 0.1364 t per barrel (a design conversion for crude of 0.858 t/m³): 0.327 / 1.637 / 12.14 Mt. One province's distribution, not a global model.

PLACEHOLDERS (not found): density_per_1e5km2 5 / 20 / 160 fields per 100,000 km² of charged-trap area, min_separation_m 2000, formation_depth_m 2000; ore_density_t_m3 0.13 is oil tonnes per m³ of reservoir rock (20 % porosity × 75 % oil saturation × 0.85 t/m³, a design value), so the dome is the reservoir's volume.

Design values: migration_km 50, the trap/seal/reservoir thresholds, min_source 1 wt% TOC, min_kitchen_km2 500 (about 22 L1 cells: a real history has thousands of one-cell hot spots that are not generative basins), the gas/oil/water legs; a layer generates only while hotter than 80 °C (petroleum.rs).
erosion_behavior destroy: erosion into a trap breaches it. Fluids place no blocks (ore_block_policy none); the charge goes to CDG (P1-16) as cdg_charge_mb = oil tonnes / 0.85 t/m³ × 1000.

cdg_scale 0.02 (P1-16, a gameplay value, judged): CDG sees 2 % of the physical charge, split over the trap's chunks by the dome's volume in each, so a chunk holds a few million mB like CDG's own oil chunks (threshold 4,000,000, infinite above 10,000,000 by default) and the thickest chunks of large traps reach CDG's infinite threshold.

Assessment depth 10 km, i.e. every trap in the build range counts: USGS petroleum assessments have no fixed depth cut-off (each assessment unit carries its own drilling depths; deep gas is counted below 4.5 km, Dyman et al. 2002, Nat. Resour. Res. 11:207). Counts (survivor formula, decisions log 2026-09-29, plan §8.6 as built): the density counts deposits that survive to the present, as USGS does; the engine forms more (deposits/survival.rs) so that the expected survivors are ρ_p50 · permissive area · count_mult. balance.count_mult stays 1: a pack lever, not a calibration. Formation is the trap's charge; a trap that erosion reaches is breached (erosion_behavior destroy), so about three quarters of those charged survive.
